segments.spokenText: IELTS Academic practice. Mock 8. Listening. You will hear each part once. Write your answers on the answer sheet. There are four parts and forty questions.
Part 1. Joining a neighbourhood walking group. You now have one minute to read questions 1 to 10.
Hello, Green Routes walking group. You're speaking to Max.
segments.sourceText: Hello, Green Routes walking group. You’re speaking to Max.

segments.spokenText: Hello. I'd like to join one of your weekend walks. I saw a leaflet at the health centre, but it listed several groups and I wasn't sure which one was suitable. I walk to work, though I haven't done anything long in the countryside recently.
segments.sourceText: Hello. I’d like to join one of your weekend walks. I saw a leaflet at the health centre, but it listed several groups and I wasn’t sure which one was suitable. I walk to work, though I haven’t done anything long in the countryside recently.

segments.spokenText: Our introductory route would be a sensible start. It's mostly level and has places to stop. Could I take your name first? We keep a list so that the leader knows whom to expect, but we don't ask for medical details on the telephone.
segments.sourceText: Our introductory route would be a sensible start. It’s mostly level and has places to stop. Could I take your name first? We keep a list so that the leader knows whom to expect, but we don’t ask for medical details on the telephone.

segments.spokenText: It's Joel Ashby. That's A, S, H, B, Y. My cousin has the same surname with an extra letter, so I usually spell it. Is there an annual membership payment?
segments.sourceText: It’s Joel Ashby. That’s A-S-H-B-Y. My cousin has the same surname with an extra letter, so I usually spell it. Is there an annual membership payment?

segments.spokenText: There is for the longer programme, but your first walk costs nothing. You can decide about joining afterwards. The next introductory one is on Sunday. We used to run it on Saturday, but the leader now works then.
segments.sourceText: There is for the longer programme, but your first walk costs nothing. You can decide about joining afterwards. The next introductory one is on Sunday. We used to run it on Saturday, but the leader now works then.

segments.spokenText: Sunday is better for me anyway. Where do you meet? The leaflet mentioned the station.
segments.sourceText: Sunday is better for me anyway. Where do you meet? The leaflet mentioned the station.

segments.spokenText: That was the starting point while the footbridge was being repaired. We're back at the museum now, beside its main doors. It's easy to find from the bus stop, and there's shelter if people arrive early.
segments.sourceText: That was the starting point while the footbridge was being repaired. We’re back at the museum now, beside its main doors. It’s easy to find from the bus stop, and there’s shelter if people arrive early.

segments.spokenText: And how early is early? I prefer not to rush off a bus straight into a long walk.
segments.sourceText: And how early is early? I prefer not to rush off a bus straight into a long walk.

segments.spokenText: We gather at nine fifteen and leave at nine thirty. Put nine fifteen in your diary, because the leader gives a short briefing before departure. If you're delayed, call the number on the confirmation rather than trying to catch up alone.
segments.sourceText: We gather at nine fifteen and leave at nine thirty. Put 9:15 in your diary, because the leader gives a short briefing before departure. If you’re delayed, call the number on the confirmation rather than trying to catch up alone.

segments.spokenText: How far will we go? I can manage four kilometres comfortably, but eight might be a bit much the first time.
segments.sourceText: How far will we go? I can manage four kilometres comfortably, but eight might be a bit much the first time.

segments.spokenText: This one is six kilometres. There's a shorter return option if someone needs it, although most people complete the full route. We don't use the speed of the fastest person to set the pace. The leader stays aware of the group and a second volunteer walks at the back.

segments.spokenText: Now look at questions 6 to 10.
I own ordinary trainers. Would I need to buy boots before coming?
segments.sourceText: I own ordinary trainers. Would I need to buy boots before coming?

segments.spokenText: Not for this route if it's dry. Trainers with a good grip are fine. Please bring a waterproof, though. A forecast can change, and the riverside section has nowhere to shelter. A large umbrella is awkward on the narrow path, so a jacket is more useful.

segments.spokenText: Should I bring lunch as well?
segments.sourceText: Should I bring lunch as well?

segments.spokenText: A snack and some water. We finish near a café, but buying anything there is entirely optional. Carry a bottle rather than depending on places along the way, since the public fountain is currently out of use.

segments.spokenText: I sometimes use a walking pole. Is the path wide enough for that?
segments.sourceText: I sometimes use a walking pole. Is the path wide enough for that?

segments.spokenText: Yes. There's one section with a stile, but we use a nearby gate instead. We don't go up the steps shown on an older route map. If you have any concerns about the gate width or surface, the leader can discuss them before the day.

segments.spokenText: That sounds reassuring. Can people bring dogs? My neighbour might come, and hers is very calm.
segments.sourceText: That sounds reassuring. Can people bring dogs? My neighbour might come, and hers is very calm.

segments.spokenText: Dogs aren't permitted on this particular walk because we cross a field containing livestock. Some of our other routes welcome them. It isn't a general judgement about well-behaved dogs; it's an agreement with the farmer for this route.

segments.spokenText: Fair enough. What happens if there's severe weather? Would you call everyone?
segments.sourceText: Fair enough. What happens if there’s severe weather? Would you call everyone?

segments.spokenText: We send a text by eight that morning if we cancel. For ordinary rain the walk usually goes ahead, but strong wind near the trees is different. Please reply to acknowledge a cancellation so we know you won't travel unnecessarily. I'll send a confirmation now with the route description and the leader's contact number.

segments.spokenText: That is the end of part 1. You now have thirty seconds to check your answers.
